title: Rust: Binary Search
description: Implement binary search on sorted arrays using both iterative and recursive approaches.

steps.title: Iterative Binary Search
steps.description: Write an iterative function `binary_search(arr: &[i32], target: i32) -> Option<usize>` that returns the index of target if found. Test with `[1, 3, 5, 7, 9]` searching for 5 and 6.
hints: If arr[mid] == target return Some(mid), else adjust bounds.

steps.title: Recursive Binary Search
steps.description: Write a recursive version `binary_search_rec(arr: &[i32], target: i32, left: usize, right: usize) -> Option<usize>`. Test with the same inputs.
hints: Base case: `if left > right { return None; }`
Calculate mid, compare arr[mid] with target.
Recursively call with updated left/right bounds.

verification.failureMessage: Find 5 and 6 using recursive binary search.

steps.title: Generic Binary Search
steps.description: Make your binary search generic: `fn binary_search_gen<T: Ord>(arr: &[T], target: &T) -> Option<usize>`. Test with i32 slice and &str slice.
hints: Use `<` and `>` for comparison (requires Ord trait).

verification.failureMessage: Test with both i32 and &str slices.

steps.title: First/Last Occurrence
steps.description: Write functions `first_occurrence(arr: &[i32], target: i32) -> Option<usize>` and `last_occurrence(...)` for arrays with duplicates. Test with `[1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4]`.
hints: For first: when arr[mid] == target, set right = mid (don't return yet).
For last: when arr[mid] == target, set left = mid + 1.
Look left/right further for the boundary.

verification.failureMessage: Find first (1) and last (3) occurrence of 2 in [1,2,2,2,3,4].

steps.title: Search Insert Position
steps.description: Write a function `search_insert(nums: &[i32], target: i32) -> usize` that returns the index where target should be inserted (like LeetCode 35). Test with `[1, 3, 5, 6]`, targets 5, 2, 7, 0.
hints: If found, return the index. If not found, return the insertion position (left pointer).
The insertion point is where `left` ends up after the loop.
